problems.title: Glucose determination
problems.problem:
Problem 2 Glucose determination

A widely used method to detect aldehydes (alkanals) is the one using Fehling's reagent. Its active component is $\ce{Cu^{2+}}$.
Because glucose in the open-chain structure has an aldehyde group in the molecule, glucose reacts with Fehling's reagent. The aldehyde group in the glucose molecule is converted into a carboxylate group. The $\ce{Cu^{2+}}$ is converted into $\ce{Cu2O}$, a "brick-red" precipitate.
The reaction is carried out in a basic medium. To prevent copper(II) hydroxide from precipitating in that medium, the $\ce{Cu^{2+}}$ is first converted into a deep blue soluble complex, copper(II) ditartrate.
Fehling's reagent is prepared from two solutions: Fehling A and Fehling B; an excess of Fehling B is used.
Fehling A is a solution of copper(II) sulfate and Fehling B is a solution of potassium sodium tartrate ($\ce{KNaC4H4O6}$) and sodium hydroxide. When Fehling A and Fehling B are combined, the following reaction occurs:

$$\ce{Cu^{2+} + 2 C4H4O6^{2-} -> Cu(C4H4O6)2^{2-}}$$

The equation of the reaction that occurs when Fehling's reagent reacts with glucose is as follows (here the complex copper ion is represented as ‘$\ce{Cu^{2+}}$’):

$$\ce{C6H12O6 + 5 OH- + 2}\,\text{‘}\ce{Cu^{2+}}\text{’}\ce{{} -> C6H11O7- + Cu2O + 3 H2O}$$

This is a redox reaction.

1 Give the equation of each of the two half-reactions of this redox reaction. Also use the notation ‘$\ce{Cu^{2+}}$’ for the complex copper ion.

Irene wants to use Fehling's reagent to determine the glucose content of dextrose tablets by means of a titration. Because the $[\ce{Cu^{2+}}]$ in the Fehling A provided is not known, she first had to determine it. She did this colorimetrically.
Starting from a $0.0385\,\mathrm{M}$ standard solution of copper(II) sulfate, she prepared a calibration series of solutions with a known $[\ce{Cu^{2+}}]$ and measured their absorbances. The calibration series consists of four solutions that contain, respectively, $1.00\,\mathrm{mL}$, $2.00\,\mathrm{mL}$, $3.00\,\mathrm{mL}$ and $4.00\,\mathrm{mL}$ of the standard solution. Each of these solutions was made up with distilled water to a volume of $10.00\,\mathrm{mL}$.
She plotted the measured absorbances in a diagram, which gave the following calibration line (see next page).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-2-9-fig1.png

[Editor's note: Dutch labels in the figure: "extinctie" = absorbance (vertical axis); the horizontal axis is "mL 0,0385 M CuSO4 oplossing" = mL of $0.0385\,\mathrm{M}$ $\ce{CuSO4}$ solution.]

Then she took $10.0\,\mathrm{\mu L}$ of Fehling A, diluted it with water to $1.50\,\mathrm{mL}$ and measured the absorbance of this. It was $0.48$.

2 Calculate $[\ce{Cu^{2+}}]$ in the Fehling A.

Before carrying out the titration she added an excess of Fehling B to the Fehling A and diluted the resulting Fehling's reagent with water until the molarity of the $\ce{Cu(C4H4O6)2^{2-}}$ was equal to $0.123\,\mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}}$. She transferred $70.0\,\mathrm{mL}$ of this Fehling's reagent into an Erlenmeyer flask.
Then she finely ground a dextrose tablet of $2.52\,\mathrm{g}$ and dissolved it in distilled water to a volume of $40.0\,\mathrm{mL}$. With this solution she titrated the $70.0\,\mathrm{mL}$ of her Fehling's reagent. As indicator she used methylene blue. When all the ‘$\ce{Cu^{2+}}$’ has reacted, the colour of the indicator changes from blue to colourless, because the glucose then reacts with the methylene blue. The end point of the titration was reached after adding $13.05\,\mathrm{mL}$ of the solution of the dextrose tablet.

3 Calculate the mass percentage of glucose in the dextrose tablet examined.

On reflection, Irene found that it had not been necessary to first determine the molarity of the Fehling A.

4 Explain whether you agree with Irene.

According to Suzanne it is not necessary at all to know the content of the Fehling's reagent. She carried out two titrations. In the first titration she titrated a certain amount of Fehling's reagent with a standard glucose solution of which the glucose concentration, $c_\mathrm{st}$, was known. Of this, $v_\mathrm{st}$ mL was needed. Then she titrated the same amount of Fehling's reagent with the solution of the dextrose tablet. Of this, $v_\mathrm{d}$ mL was needed.

5 Give a formula with which, using both titration results, you can calculate the glucose concentration, $c_\mathrm{d}$, in the solution of the dextrose tablet.
problems.problem_orig:
Opgave 2 Glucosebepaling

Een veel gebruikte methode om aldehyden (alkanalen) aan te tonen, is die met behulp van Fehlingsreagens. Het werkzame bestanddeel hiervan is $\ce{Cu^{2+}}$.
Omdat glucose in de open ketenstructuur een aldehydegroep in het molecuul bezit, reageert glucose met Fehlingsreagens. De aldehydegroep in het glucosemolecuul wordt daarbij omgezet tot een carboxylaatgroep. Het $\ce{Cu^{2+}}$ wordt omgezet tot $\ce{Cu2O}$, een ‘steenrood’ neerslag.
De reactie wordt uitgevoerd in basisch milieu. Om te verhinderen dat in dat milieu koper(II)hydroxide neerslaat, wordt het $\ce{Cu^{2+}}$ eerst omgezet tot een diepblauw oplosbaar complex van koper(II)ditartraat.
Fehlingsreagens wordt bereid uit twee oplossingen: Fehling A en Fehling B; er wordt overmaat Fehling B gebruikt.
Fehling A is een oplossing van koper(II)sulfaat en Fehling B is een oplossing van kaliumnatriumtartraat ($\ce{KNaC4H4O6}$) en natriumhydroxide. Bij samenvoegen van Fehling A en Fehling B treedt de volgende reactie op:

$$\ce{Cu^{2+} + 2 C4H4O6^{2-} -> Cu(C4H4O6)2^{2-}}$$

De vergelijking van de reactie die optreedt als Fehlingsreagens met glucose reageert, is als volgt (hierin is het complexe koperion als ‘$\ce{Cu^{2+}}$’ weergegeven):

$$\ce{C6H12O6 + 5 OH- + 2}\,\text{‘}\ce{Cu^{2+}}\text{’}\ce{{} -> C6H11O7- + Cu2O + 3 H2O}$$

Dit is een redoxreactie.

1 Geef van beide halfreacties van deze redoxreactie de vergelijking. Gebruik ook de notatie ‘$\ce{Cu^{2+}}$’ voor het complexe koperion.

Irene wil Fehlingsreagens gebruiken om door middel van een titratie het gehalte aan glucose in dextrosetabletten te bepalen. Omdat de $[\ce{Cu^{2+}}]$ in het verstrekte Fehling A niet bekend is, moest zij die eerst bepalen. Dat heeft ze colorimetrisch gedaan.
Ze heeft, uitgaande van een $0{,}0385\,\mathrm{M}$ standaardoplossing van koper(II)sulfaat een ijkreeks van oplossingen met een bekende $[\ce{Cu^{2+}}]$ gemaakt en daarvan de extincties gemeten. De ijkreeks bestaat uit vier oplossingen die achtereenvolgens $1{,}00\,\mathrm{mL}$, $2{,}00\,\mathrm{mL}$, $3{,}00\,\mathrm{mL}$ en $4{,}00\,\mathrm{mL}$ van de standaardoplossing bevatten. Elk van deze oplossingen is met gedestilleerd water aangevuld tot een volume van $10{,}00\,\mathrm{mL}$.
De gemeten extincties heeft ze uitgezet in een diagram, waarbij ze de volgende ijklijn heeft verkregen (zie volgende pagina).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-2-9-fig1.png

Daarna heeft ze $10{,}0\,\mathrm{\mu L}$ Fehling A genomen, dit met water verdund tot $1{,}50\,\mathrm{mL}$ en hiervan de extinctie gemeten. Deze bedroeg $0{,}48$.

2 Bereken $[\ce{Cu^{2+}}]$ in het Fehling A.

Voorafgaand aan het uitvoeren van de titratie heeft ze aan het Fehling A een overmaat Fehling B toegevoegd en het ontstane Fehlingsreagens met water verdund tot de molariteit van het $\ce{Cu(C4H4O6)2^{2-}}$ gelijk was aan $0{,}123\,\mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}}$. Van dit Fehlingsreagens heeft ze $70{,}0\,\mathrm{mL}$ overgebracht in een erlenmeyer.
Daarna heeft ze een dextrosetablet van $2{,}52\,\mathrm{g}$ fijngemalen en opgelost in gedestilleerd water tot een volume van $40{,}0\,\mathrm{mL}$. Met deze oplossing heeft ze de $70{,}0\,\mathrm{mL}$ van haar Fehlingsreagens getitreerd. Als indicator heeft ze methyleenblauw gebruikt. Als alle ‘$\ce{Cu^{2+}}$’ heeft gereageerd, verandert de kleur van de indicator van blauw naar kleurloos doordat de glucose dan reageert met het methyleenblauw. Het eindpunt van de titratie was bereikt na het toevoegen van $13{,}05\,\mathrm{mL}$ van de oplossing van het dextrosetablet.

3 Bereken het massapercentage glucose in het onderzochte dextrosetablet.

Bij nader inzien vond Irene dat het niet nodig was om eerst de molariteit van het Fehling A te bepalen.

4 Leg uit of je het met Irene eens bent.

Volgens Suzanne is het helemaal niet nodig om het gehalte van het Fehlingsreagens te weten. Zij heeft twee titraties uitgevoerd. In de eerste titratie heeft ze een bepaalde hoeveelheid Fehlingsreagens getitreerd met een standaardglucose-oplossing waarvan de glucoseconcentratie, $c_\mathrm{st}$, bekend was. Daarvan was $v_\mathrm{st}$ mL nodig. Vervolgens titreerde ze een zelfde hoeveelheid Fehlingsreagens met de oplossing van het dextrosetablet. Daarvan was $v_\mathrm{d}$ mL nodig.

5 Geef een formule waarmee je met behulp van de beide titratieresultaten de glucoseconcentratie, $c_\mathrm{d}$, in de oplossing van het dextrosetablet kunt berekenen.

problems.title: The Mond process
problems.problem:
Problem 3 The Mond process

Nickel is obtained, among other sources, from the ore pentlandite. Pentlandite can be represented by the formula $\ce{Fe4Ni5S8}$. In the industrial preparation of nickel from pentlandite, the pentlandite is first converted by reaction with oxygen into nickel(II) oxide. Iron(III) oxide and sulfur dioxide are also formed.

6 Give the equation of this reaction.

The Mond process is used for the industrial preparation of very pure nickel. A description of this continuous process follows.
• The mixture of solids that was formed in the reaction of pentlandite with oxygen is allowed to react with hydrogen at a temperature of $473\,\mathrm{K}$ in a reactor (R1). An excess of hydrogen is used. Crude nickel is formed. Water vapour is also formed. The crude nickel still contains many impurities.
• The gas mixture of water vapour and unreacted hydrogen is cooled in a separation chamber S.
• The crude nickel is taken to a next reactor (R2). There it is allowed to react with carbon monoxide. An excess of carbon monoxide is constantly present in this reactor. The temperature in this reactor is $330\,\mathrm{K}$. All of the nickel is converted in this reactor into nickel tetracarbonyl, a gas with formula $\ce{Ni(CO)4}$. Only the nickel from the crude nickel reacts with carbon monoxide. The other solid components are removed as waste.
• The nickel tetracarbonyl and the excess carbon monoxide are led to a third reactor (R3). There, at a temperature of $500\,\mathrm{K}$, all of the nickel tetracarbonyl is converted into nickel and carbon monoxide. The nickel formed is very pure.

An incomplete block flow diagram of this process is shown below. In it, the mixture of solids that was formed in the reaction of pentlandite with oxygen is represented as crude nickel oxide.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-2-10-fig1.png

[Editor's note: Dutch labels in the figure: "ruw nikkeloxide" = crude nickel oxide; "ruw nikkel" = crude nickel.]

7 Copy this part of the block flow diagram and extend it to a complete block flow diagram for the continuous process after the start-up phase.
• Place blocks for the separation chamber S and the reactors R2 and R3.
• Draw the missing material streams; take into account the reuse of substances.
• Add names or formulas to the missing material streams.

8 Explain by means of a calculation whether iron can also be formed at the temperature in reactor R1. Assume that data from Binas or ScienceData can be used under these conditions.

The formation of nickel tetracarbonyl is an equilibrium reaction:

$$\ce{Ni(s) + 4 CO(g) <=> Ni(CO)4(g)}$$

For the reaction to the right:
$\Delta_r H = -165\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ and $\Delta_r S = -405\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$.

9 Show by means of a calculation of the equilibrium constant that the above equilibrium lies extremely far to the left in reactor R3. Assume that $\Delta_r H$ and $\Delta_r S$ are independent of temperature.
problems.problem_orig:
Opgave 3 Het Mondproces

Nikkel wordt onder andere verkregen uit het erts pentlandiet. Pentlandiet kan worden weergegeven met de formule $\ce{Fe4Ni5S8}$. Bij de industriële bereiding van nikkel uit pentlandiet wordt het pentlandiet eerst door reactie met zuurstof omgezet tot nikkel(II)oxide. Tevens ontstaan ijzer(III)oxide en zwaveldioxide.

6 Geef de vergelijking van deze reactie.

Voor de industriële bereiding van zeer zuiver nikkel wordt het Mondproces gebruikt. Hieronder volgt een beschrijving van dit continuproces.
• Het mengsel van vaste stoffen dat bij de reactie van pentlandiet met zuurstof is ontstaan, laat men bij een temperatuur van $473\,\mathrm{K}$ in een reactor (R1) met waterstof reageren. Er wordt overmaat waterstof gebruikt. Er ontstaat ruw nikkel. Tevens ontstaat waterdamp. Het ruwe nikkel bevat nog veel verontreinigingen.
• Het gasmengsel van waterdamp en niet-gereageerd waterstof wordt in een scheidingsruimte S afgekoeld.
• Het ruwe nikkel wordt naar een volgende reactor (R2) gebracht. Daar laat men het reageren met koolstofmonoöxide. In deze reactor is constant overmaat koolstofmonoöxide aanwezig. De temperatuur in deze reactor is $330\,\mathrm{K}$. Alle nikkel wordt in deze reactor omgezet tot nikkeltetracarbonyl, een gas met formule $\ce{Ni(CO)4}$. Alleen het nikkel uit het ruwe nikkel reageert met koolstofmonoöxide. De overige vaste bestanddelen worden als afval afgevoerd.
• Het nikkeltetracarbonyl en de overmaat koolstofmonoöxide worden naar een derde reactor (R3) geleid. Daar wordt bij een temperatuur van $500\,\mathrm{K}$ alle nikkeltetracarbonyl omgezet tot nikkel en koolstofmonoöxide. Het ontstane nikkel is zeer zuiver.

Een onvolledig blokschema voor dit proces is hieronder weergegeven. Hierin is het mengsel van vaste stoffen dat bij de reactie van pentlandiet met zuurstof is ontstaan weergegeven met ruw nikkeloxide.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-2-10-fig1.png

7 Neem dit deel van het blokschema over en breid het uit tot een compleet blokschema voor het continuproces na de opstartfase.
• Plaats blokken voor de scheidingsruimte S en de reactoren R2 en R3.
• Teken de ontbrekende stofstromen; houd daarbij rekening met hergebruik van stoffen.
• Zet namen of formules bij de ontbrekende stofstromen.

8 Leg uit door middel van een berekening of bij de temperatuur in reactor R1 ook ijzer kan ontstaan. Ga ervan uit dat gegevens uit Binas of ScienceData onder deze omstandigheden kunnen worden gebruikt.

De vorming van nikkeltetracarbonyl is een evenwichtsreactie:

$$\ce{Ni(s) + 4 CO(g) <=> Ni(CO)4(g)}$$

Voor de reactie naar rechts geldt:
$\Delta_r H = -165\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$ en $\Delta_r S = -405\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$.

9 Laat met behulp van een berekening van de evenwichtsconstante zien dat bovengenoemd evenwicht in reactor R3 uiterst links ligt. Ga ervan uit dat $\Delta_r H$ en $\Delta_r S$ niet afhankelijk zijn van de temperatuur.

A recently developed synthesis of molnupiravir is shown schematically below. In this synthesis uridine is the starting material.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-2-11-fig2.png

[Editor's note: Dutch labels in the scheme: "opbrengst" = yield; "molnupiravir 69% opbrengst vanaf 3" = molnupiravir, 69% yield from 3.]

In the first step of the synthesis uridine is converted into $\mathbf{1}$. This conversion can be regarded as an addition reaction in which intermediate $\mathbf{X}$ is formed, followed by an elimination reaction in which, besides $\mathbf{1}$, substance $\mathbf{Y}$ is also formed from intermediate $\mathbf{X}$.

10 Give the structural formulas of $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$.

Because in a molecule of $\mathbf{1}$ only one specific OH group has to be converted into an ester group, the two other OH groups are first protected by reaction with 2,2-dimethoxypropane. This protection is undone in the last step of the synthesis.
In the reaction of $\mathbf{Z}$ with $\mathbf{2}$, 2-methylpropanoic acid is formed as a by-product.

11 Give the structural formula of $\mathbf{Z}$.

The conversion of $\mathbf{3}$ into $\mathbf{4}$ takes place by reaction with hydroxylamine ($\ce{NH2OH}$).
In this reaction the substance with the following structural formula is released.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-2-11-fig3.png

12 Copy the following sentence and choose the correct term from the terms printed in italics.
The conversion of $\mathbf{3}$ into $\mathbf{4}$ is an $\textit{electrophilic/nucleophilic}$ $\textit{addition reaction/substitution reaction}$.

The removal of the protecting group in the last step of the synthesis, in which $\mathbf{4}$ is converted into molnupiravir and 2,2-dimethoxypropane, takes place in methanol with sulfuric acid as catalyst.
The mechanism of this reaction proceeds as follows:
1. One of the ether groups is protonated.
2. One of the C — O bonds is broken, whereby an OH group is formed on the five-membered ring.
3. Reaction of a methanol molecule at the C position of the broken C — O bond.
4. Loss of $\ce{H+}$.
And further: repetition of 1 to 4 for the other ether group.

13 Show steps 1 to 4 of the mechanism with structural formulas:
• Start from the following part of $\mathbf{4}$

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-2-11-fig4.png

• Draw all bonding and non-bonding electron pairs.
• Use curved arrows [a curved-arrow symbol is printed here] to indicate how electron pairs shift during the formation and breaking of bonds.
• Place all formal charges in the right position.

Compared with other syntheses of molnupiravir, the synthesis above has a high yield.

14 Calculate how many grams of molnupiravir are formed from $1.0\,\mathrm{g}$ of uridine.
Use:
• the molar mass of uridine ($244.2\,\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$) and of molnupiravir ($329.3\,\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$);
• the yields given in the scheme.

The antiviral action of molnupiravir is based on disturbing the reproduction of the virus RNA. After a virus particle has entered a host cell, the virus RNA is released into the cell contents and starts to reproduce. In this way more virus RNA is formed and the multiplication of virus particles can take place.
Figure 1 shows schematically how the reproduction of virus RNA normally proceeds. The letters represent the known nucleobases.

figure 1

$$\begin{array}{lll} \text{virus RNA} & \text{(+) strand} & \cdots\ \mathrm{G\ C\ G\ A\ C\ U}\ \cdots \\ & \text{(}-\text{) strand} & \cdots\ \mathrm{C\ G\ C\ U\ G\ A}\ \cdots \\ & \text{(+) strand} & \cdots\ \mathrm{G\ C\ G\ A\ C\ U}\ \cdots \\ & & \text{and so on} \end{array}$$

A complementary strand of RNA (the ($-$) strand) is formed on the virus RNA (the (+) strand). Both strands are connected to each other by hydrogen bonds between the usual base pairs (C — G and A — U). After the strands have been separated, a (+) strand is again formed on the ($-$) strand, and so on.
When molnupiravir has been administered, changes, so-called mutations, occur in the reproduction of virus RNA. Such mutations lead to inhibition of the reproduction and even to the "death" of the virus.
By the incorporation of molnupiravir monophosphate in place of cytosine monophosphate during reproduction, a mutation from G to A can arise.
This mutation from G to A can be represented schematically as follows; here the base group in molnupiravir is represented by M:

figure 2

$$\begin{array}{lll} \text{virus RNA} & \text{(+) strand} & \cdots\ \mathrm{G\ C\ G\ A\ C\ U}\ \cdots \\ & \text{(}-\text{) strand} & \cdots\ \mathrm{C\ G}\ \boxed{\mathrm{M}}\ \mathrm{U\ G\ A}\ \cdots \\ & \text{(+) strand} & \cdots\ \mathrm{G\ C}\ \boxed{\mathrm{A}}\ \mathrm{A\ C\ U}\ \cdots \end{array}$$

This mutation is possible because M can form hydrogen bonds with guanine (G) as well as with adenine (A).
An M unit forms three hydrogen bonds with a G unit.

15 Show how a G unit is coupled with an M unit.
• Show the three hydrogen bonds with dotted lines ( - - - - ).
• Use Binas tables 71 A and B or ScienceData table 16.3.
• Write the M unit as

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-2-11-fig5.png

Molnupiravir can also cause mutations from C to U in the virus RNA.

16 Draw schematically how a mutation from C to U can take place in the reproduction of virus RNA in the presence of molnupiravir.
• Draw the scheme in a way similar to figures 1 and 2.
• Begin your drawing with: (+) strand $\cdots\ \mathrm{C}\ \cdots$

Opgave 4 Molnupiravir

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-2-11-fig1.png

Molnupiravir is een antiviraal geneesmiddel dat recent is goedgekeurd voor de behandeling van COVID-19. Molnupiravir wordt in pilvorm toegediend in een vroeg stadium van de ziekte.
Een recent ontwikkelde synthese van molnupiravir is hieronder schematisch weergegeven. In deze synthese is uridine de beginstof.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-2-11-fig2.png

In de eerste stap van de synthese wordt uridine omgezet tot $\mathbf{1}$. Deze omzetting is op te vatten als een additiereactie, waarbij tussenproduct $\mathbf{X}$ wordt gevormd, gevolgd door een eliminatiereactie waarbij uit tussenproduct $\mathbf{X}$ behalve $\mathbf{1}$ ook stof $\mathbf{Y}$ ontstaat.

10 Geef de structuurformules van $\mathbf{X}$ en $\mathbf{Y}$.

Omdat in een molecuul $\mathbf{1}$ slechts één specifieke OH groep moet worden omgezet tot een estergroep, worden de twee andere OH groepen eerst beschermd door reactie met 2,2-dimethoxypropaan. Deze bescherming wordt in de laatste stap van de synthese ongedaan gemaakt.
Bij de reactie van $\mathbf{Z}$ met $\mathbf{2}$ ontstaat 2-methylpropaanzuur als bijproduct.

11 Geef de structuurformule van $\mathbf{Z}$.

De omzetting van $\mathbf{3}$ tot $\mathbf{4}$ vindt plaats door reactie met hydroxylamine ($\ce{NH2OH}$).
Bij deze reactie komt de stof met de volgende structuurformule vrij.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-2-11-fig3.png

12 Neem de volgende zin over en kies daarin het juiste begrip uit de cursief gedrukte begrippen.
De omzetting van $\mathbf{3}$ tot $\mathbf{4}$ is een $\textit{elektrofiele/nucleofiele}$ $\textit{additiereactie/substitutiereactie}$.

De verwijdering van de beschermende groep in de laatste stap van de synthese, waarin $\mathbf{4}$ wordt omgezet tot molnupiravir en 2,2-dimethoxypropaan, vindt plaats in methanol met zwavelzuur als katalysator.
Het mechanisme van deze reactie verloopt als volgt:
1. Eén van de ethergroepen wordt geprotoneerd.
2. Eén van de C — O bindingen wordt verbroken waarbij aan de vijfring een OH groep ontstaat.
3. Reactie van een methanolmolecuul op de C positie van de verbroken C — O binding.
4. Afsplitsing van $\ce{H+}$.
En verder: herhaling van 1 tot en met 4 bij de andere ethergroep.

13 Geef de stappen 1 tot en met 4 van het mechanisme weer in structuurformules:
• Ga uit van het volgende onderdeel van $\mathbf{4}$

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-2-11-fig4.png

• Teken alle bindende en niet-bindende elektronenparen.
• Geef met kromme pijlen [a curved-arrow symbol is printed here] aan hoe elektronenparen verschuiven bij het vormen en verbreken van bindingen.
• Zet alle formele ladingen op de juiste positie.

Vergeleken met andere syntheses van molnupiravir heeft de bovenstaande synthese een hoge opbrengst.

14 Bereken hoeveel gram molnupiravir wordt gevormd uit $1{,}0\,\mathrm{g}$ uridine.
Maak hierbij gebruik van:
• de molaire massa van uridine ($244{,}2\,\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$) en van molnupiravir ($329{,}3\,\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$);
• de rendementen die in het schema zijn vermeld.

De antivirale werking van molnupiravir berust op de verstoring van de reproductie van het virusRNA. Na het binnendringen van een virusdeeltje in een gastheercel komt het virusRNA vrij in de celinhoud en gaat zich reproduceren. Zo wordt meer virusRNA gevormd en kan de vermeerdering van virusdeeltjes plaatsvinden.
In figuur 1 is schematisch weergegeven hoe de reproductie van virusRNA normaal verloopt. De letters geven de bekende nucleïnebasen weer.

figuur 1

$$\begin{array}{lll} \text{virusRNA} & \text{(+) streng} & \cdots\ \mathrm{G\ C\ G\ A\ C\ U}\ \cdots \\ & \text{(}-\text{) streng} & \cdots\ \mathrm{C\ G\ C\ U\ G\ A}\ \cdots \\ & \text{(+) streng} & \cdots\ \mathrm{G\ C\ G\ A\ C\ U}\ \cdots \\ & & \text{enzovoorts} \end{array}$$

Aan het virusRNA (de (+) streng) wordt een complementaire streng RNA (de ($-$) streng) gevormd. Beide strengen worden via waterstofbruggen tussen de gebruikelijke basenparen (C — G en A — U) met elkaar verbonden. Na ontkoppeling van de strengen wordt aan de ($-$) streng weer een (+) streng gevormd, enzovoorts.
Wanneer molnupiravir is toegediend, ontstaan bij de reproductie van virusRNA veranderingen, zogenoemde mutaties. Dergelijke mutaties leiden tot de remming van de reproductie en zelfs tot de “dood” van het virus.
Door de inbouw van molnupiravirmonofosfaat in de plaats van cytosinemonofosfaat bij de reproductie kan een mutatie van G naar A ontstaan.
Deze mutatie van G naar A kan als volgt schematisch worden weergegeven; hierin is de basegroep in molnupiravir met M weergegeven:

figuur 2

$$\begin{array}{lll} \text{virusRNA} & \text{(+) streng} & \cdots\ \mathrm{G\ C\ G\ A\ C\ U}\ \cdots \\ & \text{(}-\text{) streng} & \cdots\ \mathrm{C\ G}\ \boxed{\mathrm{M}}\ \mathrm{U\ G\ A}\ \cdots \\ & \text{(+) streng} & \cdots\ \mathrm{G\ C}\ \boxed{\mathrm{A}}\ \mathrm{A\ C\ U}\ \cdots \end{array}$$

Deze mutatie is mogelijk doordat M zowel met guanine (G) als met adenine (A) waterstofbruggen kan vormen.
Een M — eenheid vormt drie waterstofbruggen met G — eenheid.

15 Geef weer hoe een G — eenheid is gekoppeld met een M — eenheid.
• Geef hierin de drie waterstofbruggen weer met stippellijntjes ( - - - - ).
• Maak gebruik van Binas-tabellen 71 A en B of ScienceData-tabel 16.3.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-2-11-fig5.png

Molnupiravir kan ook mutaties van C naar U in het virusRNA veroorzaken.

problems.title: Pyrite
problems.problem:
Problem 1 Pyrite

Pyrite is a mineral with the formula $\ce{FeS2}$. In the cubic unit cell of pyrite, the $\ce{Fe^{2+}}$ ions are face-centred: they are located at the corners of the cube and in the middle of the faces. The density of pyrite is $5.01\cdot10^{3}\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$.

1 Calculate the smallest distance in pm (picometres) between the nuclei of two $\ce{Fe^{2+}}$ ions in pyrite.

Naturally occurring pyrite does not have exactly the formula $\ce{FeS2}$. This is because part of the $\ce{S2^{2-}}$ ions has been replaced by $\ce{S^{2-}}$ ions. Pyrite is thus a mixture of $\ce{FeS2}$ and a little $\ce{FeS}$. The formula of pyrite can then be represented by $\mathrm{FeS}_{2-x}$.

To determine how large $x$ is in $\mathrm{FeS}_{2-x}$, a certain amount of pyrite was treated with a solution of bromine in potassium hydroxide solution. The following conversions took place:

$$\ce{FeS2(s) + Br2(aq) + OH-(aq) -> Fe(OH)3(s) + Br-(aq) + SO4^{2-}(aq) + H2O(l)} \qquad (1)$$

and

$$\ce{FeS(s) + Br2(aq) + OH-(aq) -> Fe(OH)3(s) + Br-(aq) + SO4^{2-}(aq) + H2O(l)} \qquad (2)$$

In the incomplete reaction equations above only the coefficients are missing.

The solids were filtered off and ignited (strongly heated). This gave $0.2000\,\mathrm{g}$ of iron(III) oxide.

An excess of barium chloride solution was added to the filtrate. This gave $1.1087\,\mathrm{g}$ of barium sulfate.

2 Calculate $x$ in $\mathrm{FeS}_{2-x}$.

3 Write a balanced equation for conversion (1).
problems.problem_orig:
Opgave 1 Pyriet

Pyriet is een mineraal met de formule $\ce{FeS2}$. In de kubische eenheidscel van pyriet zijn de $\ce{Fe^{2+}}$ ionen vlakgecentreerd geplaatst: ze bevinden zich op de hoekpunten van de kubus en midden op de zijvlakken. De dichtheid van pyriet is $5{,}01\cdot10^{3}\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$.

1 Bereken de kleinste afstand in pm (picometer) tussen de kernen van twee $\ce{Fe^{2+}}$ ionen in pyriet.

Natuurlijk voorkomend pyriet heeft niet exact de formule $\ce{FeS2}$. Dat komt omdat een deel van de $\ce{S2^{2-}}$ ionen is vervangen door $\ce{S^{2-}}$ ionen. Pyriet is dus een mengsel van $\ce{FeS2}$ en een beetje $\ce{FeS}$. De formule van pyriet kan dan met $\mathrm{FeS}_{2-x}$ worden weergegeven.

Om te bepalen hoe groot $x$ is in $\mathrm{FeS}_{2-x}$, is een bepaalde hoeveelheid pyriet met een oplossing van broom in kaliloog behandeld. De volgende omzettingen traden op:

$$\ce{FeS2(s) + Br2(aq) + OH-(aq) -> Fe(OH)3(s) + Br-(aq) + SO4^{2-}(aq) + H2O(l)} \qquad (1)$$

en

$$\ce{FeS(s) + Br2(aq) + OH-(aq) -> Fe(OH)3(s) + Br-(aq) + SO4^{2-}(aq) + H2O(l)} \qquad (2)$$

In bovenstaande onvolledige reactievergelijkingen ontbreken uitsluitend de coëfficiënten.

De vaste bestanddelen werden afgefiltreerd en gegloeid (sterk verhit). Daarbij ontstond $0{,}2000\,\mathrm{g}$ ijzer(III)oxide.

Aan het filtraat werd een overmaat van een bariumchloride-oplossing toegevoegd. Daarbij ontstond $1{,}1087\,\mathrm{g}$ bariumsulfaat.

2 Bereken $x$ in $\mathrm{FeS}_{2-x}$.

3 Maak van omzetting (1) een kloppende reactievergelijking.

problems.title: Argentometry with Volhard
problems.problem:
Problem 2 Argentometry with Volhard

The content of silver ions in a solution can be determined by means of the Volhard titration. In this method a solution containing $\ce{Ag+}$ is acidified and titrated with a solution of potassium thiocyanate, KSCN. The following precipitation reaction then takes place:

$$\ce{Ag+(aq) + SCN-(aq) <=> AgSCN(s)} \qquad \text{equilibrium 1}$$

$\ce{Fe^{3+}}$ is used as the indicator; at the slightest excess of thiocyanate it gives the solution a red colour, because the following reaction takes place:

$$\ce{Fe^{3+}(aq) + SCN-(aq) <=> Fe(SCN)^{2+}(aq)} \qquad \text{equilibrium 2}$$

$\ce{FeSCN^{2+}}$ ions are in fact complex ions $\ce{Fe(H2O)5(SCN)^{2+}}$. These ions have an octahedral structure. The splitting of the $d$ orbitals in such a complex can be represented as follows:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-3-2-fig1.png

4 Explain why in an octahedral complex two $d$ orbitals have a higher energy than the other three $d$ orbitals.

$\ce{Fe(H2O)5(SCN)^{2+}}$ ions give a solution a red colour because they absorb light with a wavelength of $447\,\mathrm{nm}$.

5 Calculate the ligand field splitting energy $\Delta_\mathrm{o}$, in $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$, for $\ce{Fe(H2O)5(SCN)^{2+}}$ ions.

6 Copy the splitting diagram above for the complex $\ce{Fe(H2O)5(SCN)^{2+}}$ and draw in it the electron configuration of this complex. Assume that this is a low-spin complex.

In the remainder of this problem, $\ce{Fe(SCN)^{2+}}$ is used as the formula of the complex.

It has been established that the red colour of $\ce{Fe(SCN)^{2+}}$ is clearly visible when $[\ce{Fe(SCN)^{2+}}] = 6.4\cdot10^{-6}\,\mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}}$. With this information it is possible to calculate how large $[\ce{Fe^{3+}}]$ must be at the equivalence point of a Volhard titration.

At the equivalence point of the titration the following must hold: $[\ce{Ag+}] = [\ce{SCN-}] + [\ce{Fe(SCN)^{2+}}]$.

7 Explain this.

8 Calculate $[\ce{Fe^{3+}}]$ at the equivalence point of the Volhard titration. Use data from your table book; assume $298\,\mathrm{K}$.

In a determination of the purity of a sample of silver nitrate, $4.00\,\mathrm{g}$ of the sample was dissolved in water in a volumetric flask to a volume of $100.0\,\mathrm{mL}$. From this, $10.00\,\mathrm{mL}$ was pipetted into a conical flask. After acidifying the solution, it was titrated with a $0.0823\,\mathrm{M}$ solution of KSCN. After addition of $28.4\,\mathrm{mL}$ of this solution the equivalence point was reached.

9 Calculate the mass percentage of $\ce{AgNO3}$ in the sample investigated.

Usually, because of the colour of $\ce{Fe^{3+}}$, less indicator is added than follows from the calculation of question 8. But the amount of indicator added must not be much smaller. Otherwise an incorrect result is obtained.

10 Would a result that is too high or too low be obtained in the silver nitrate determination if too little indicator were added? Give an explanation for your answer.

The Volhard titration can also be used to carry out chloride determinations. In this way the titration can be applied to determine the NaCl content of a mixture that contains NaCl and $\ce{Na2CO3}$ as main components.

11 Describe how such a determination should be carried out. Assume that, apart from NaCl and $\ce{Na2CO3}$, the mixture contains only inert components.
problems.problem_orig:
Opgave 2 Argentometrie met Volhard

Het gehalte aan zilverionen in een oplossing kan worden bepaald met behulp van de Volhardtitratie. Hierbij wordt een oplossing met $\ce{Ag+}$, na aanzuren, getitreerd met een oplossing van kaliumthiocyanaat, KSCN. De volgende neerslagreactie treedt dan op:

$$\ce{Ag+(aq) + SCN-(aq) <=> AgSCN(s)} \qquad \text{evenwicht 1}$$

Als indicator wordt $\ce{Fe^{3+}}$ gebruikt, dat bij de geringste overmaat aan thiocyanaat een rode kleur aan de oplossing geeft, doordat de volgende reactie optreedt:

$$\ce{Fe^{3+}(aq) + SCN-(aq) <=> Fe(SCN)^{2+}(aq)} \qquad \text{evenwicht 2}$$

Ionen $\ce{FeSCN^{2+}}$ zijn eigenlijk complexe ionen $\ce{Fe(H2O)5(SCN)^{2+}}$. Deze ionen hebben een octaëdrische structuur. De opsplitsing van de $d$ orbitalen in zo’n complex kan als volgt worden weergegeven:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-3-2-fig1.png

4 Leg uit waarom in een octaëdrisch complex twee $d$ orbitalen een hogere energie hebben dan de drie andere $d$ orbitalen.

Ionen $\ce{Fe(H2O)5(SCN)^{2+}}$ geven aan een oplossing een rode kleur, doordat ze licht met een golflengte van $447\,\mathrm{nm}$ absorberen.

5 Bereken de ligandveldsplitsingsenergie $\Delta_\mathrm{o}$, in $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$, voor ionen $\ce{Fe(H2O)5(SCN)^{2+}}$.

6 Neem het bovenstaande opsplitsingsdiagram voor het complex $\ce{Fe(H2O)5(SCN)^{2+}}$ over en teken hierin de elektronenconfiguratie van dit complex. Ga ervan uit dat dit een laag spin complex is.

In het vervolg van deze opgave wordt $\ce{Fe(SCN)^{2+}}$ als formule voor het complex gebruikt.

Men heeft vastgesteld dat de rode kleur van het $\ce{Fe(SCN)^{2+}}$ goed zichtbaar is, wanneer $[\ce{Fe(SCN)^{2+}}] = 6{,}4\cdot10^{-6}\,\mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}}$ is. Met behulp van dit gegeven is te berekenen hoe groot de $[\ce{Fe^{3+}}]$ in het equivalentiepunt moet zijn bij een Volhardtitratie.

In het equivalentiepunt van de titratie moet gelden: $[\ce{Ag+}] = [\ce{SCN-}] + [\ce{Fe(SCN)^{2+}}]$.

7 Leg dit uit.

8 Bereken de $[\ce{Fe^{3+}}]$ in het equivalentiepunt van de Volhardtitratie. Gebruik gegevens uit je tabellenboek; ga uit van $298\,\mathrm{K}$.

Bij een bepaling van de zuiverheid van een monster zilvernitraat heeft men $4{,}00\,\mathrm{g}$ van het monster in een maatkolf met water opgelost tot een volume van $100{,}0\,\mathrm{mL}$. Hieruit is $10{,}00\,\mathrm{mL}$ gepipetteerd in een erlenmeyer. Na aanzuren van de oplossing werd getitreerd met een $0{,}0823\,\mathrm{M}$ oplossing van KSCN. Na toevoegen van $28{,}4\,\mathrm{mL}$ van deze oplossing was het equivalentiepunt bereikt.

9 Bereken het massapercentage $\ce{AgNO3}$ in het onderzochte monster.

Meestal wordt, vanwege de kleur van het $\ce{Fe^{3+}}$, minder indicator toegevoegd dan uit de berekening van vraag 8 volgt. Maar de toegevoegde hoeveelheid indicator mag niet veel kleiner zijn. Anders wordt een onjuiste uitkomst verkregen.

10 Wordt bij de zilvernitraatbepaling een te hoge of te lage uitkomst verkregen, wanneer te weinig indicator zou worden toegevoegd? Geef een verklaring voor je antwoord.

De Volhardtitratie is ook te gebruiken om chloridebepalingen uit te voeren. Zo kan deze titratie worden toegepast om van een mengsel dat als hoofdbestanddelen NaCl en $\ce{Na2CO3}$ bevat, het gehalte aan NaCl te bepalen.

11 Beschrijf hoe zo’n bepaling zou moeten worden uitgevoerd. Ga ervan uit dat het mengsel, behalve NaCl en $\ce{Na2CO3}$, alleen inerte bestanddelen bevat.

problems.title: Production of hydrogen by the decomposition of water
problems.problem:
Problem 3 Production of hydrogen by the decomposition of water

table 1 thermodynamic data at $T = 298\,\mathrm{K}$ and $p = p_0$

$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|}\hline & \ce{H2(g)} & \ce{H2O(l)} & \ce{H2O(g)} & \ce{O2(g)} \\ \hline \Delta_\mathrm{f}H^\circ\ (\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}) & 0 & -285.8 & -241.8 & 0 \\ \hline S^\circ\ (\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}) & 130.6 & 69.9 & 188.7 & 205.2 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Hydrogen gas is an important candidate as an alternative to fossil fuels. Lowering the cost and the environmental impact of the production of hydrogen gas are important challenges in this respect.

The decomposition of water is a promising technology in this field of research.

$$\ce{2 H2O(l) -> 2 H2(g) + O2(g)}$$

The decomposition of water can be carried out by the electrolysis (see figure 1) of acidified water.

figure 1 electrolysis of water

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-3-3-fig1.png

The following half-reactions take place at the electrodes:

At the cathode (electrode 1): $\ce{2 H+(aq) + 2 e- -> H2(g)}$

At the anode (electrode 2): $\ce{2 H2O(l) -> O2(g) + 4 H+(aq) + 4 e-}$

The voltage needed for the electrolysis of water ($\Delta V_\mathrm{applied}$) must be greater than the voltage that can be calculated from thermodynamic data ($\Delta V_\mathrm{theoretical}$).

12 Calculate $\Delta_\mathrm{r}G^0$ (in J per mole of hydrogen) for the formation of hydrogen by the electrolysis of water at $298\,\mathrm{K}$. Use the data of table 1 above.

If you cannot calculate this, use in the remainder of this problem the value $1.987\cdot10^{5}\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$.

13 Calculate $\Delta V_\mathrm{theoretical}$ (in V, to three decimals) from the answer to question 12.

If you cannot calculate this, use in the remainder of this problem the value $1.234\,\mathrm{V}$.

When, in the electrolysis of water, a cathode of Pt and an anode of oxidised nickel, $\mathrm{NiO}_x$, are used, the minimum voltage that must be applied ($\Delta V_\mathrm{min}$) is equal to $1.6\,\mathrm{V}$.

The difference between $\Delta V_\mathrm{min}$ and $\Delta V_\mathrm{theoretical}$ is caused by energy losses in the electrolysis.

The thermodynamic efficiency ($\eta$) of the electrolysis of water is the fraction of the power that is used for the decomposition of water.

$\eta$ can be calculated from $\Delta V_\mathrm{min}$ and $\Delta V_\mathrm{theoretical}$ and is expressed as a percentage.

14 Calculate the thermodynamic efficiency $\eta$ for the electrolysis of water using a cathode of Pt and an anode of $\mathrm{NiO}_x$.

An alternative to the electrolysis of water is the so-called photocatalytic decomposition of water. This uses a photoelectrode. This is often a semiconductor, for example $\ce{TiO2}$, that can be activated by the absorption of (sun)light.

figure 2 schematic representation of the photocatalytic decomposition of water

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-3-3-fig2.png

In an experimental set-up the production of $\ce{H2}$ was investigated:

The photoelectrode, with a surface area of $16\,\mathrm{mm^2}$, was illuminated with simulated sunlight at $T = 25\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $p = p_0$.

The power of the incident light was $1.0\,\mathrm{kW\,m^{-2}}$.

In $1.0$ hour, $0.37\,\mathrm{cm^3}$ of hydrogen was produced.

problems.problem_orig:
Opgave 3 Productie van waterstof door de ontleding van water

tabel 1 thermodynamische gegevens bij $T = 298\,\mathrm{K}$ en $p = p_0$

$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|}\hline & \ce{H2(g)} & \ce{H2O(l)} & \ce{H2O(g)} & \ce{O2(g)} \\ \hline \Delta_\mathrm{f}H^\circ\ (\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}) & 0 & -285{,}8 & -241{,}8 & 0 \\ \hline S^\circ\ (\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}) & 130{,}6 & 69{,}9 & 188{,}7 & 205{,}2 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

Waterstofgas is een belangrijke kandidaat als alternatief voor fossiele brandstoffen. Het verlagen van de kostprijs en de milieu-impact van de productie van waterstofgas zijn daarbij belangrijke uitdagingen.

De ontleding van water is een veelbelovende technologie in dit onderzoeksgebied.

$$\ce{2 H2O(l) -> 2 H2(g) + O2(g)}$$

De ontleding van water kan worden uitgevoerd door de elektrolyse (zie figuur 1) van aangezuurd water.

figuur 1 elektrolyse van water

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-3-3-fig1.png

Aan de elektroden vinden de volgende halfreacties plaats:

Aan de kathode (elektrode 1): $\ce{2 H+(aq) + 2 e- -> H2(g)}$

Aan de anode (elektrode 2): $\ce{2 H2O(l) -> O2(g) + 4 H+(aq) + 4 e-}$

De spanning die nodig is voor de elektrolyse van water ($\Delta V_\mathrm{toegepast}$) moet groter zijn dan de spanning die kan worden berekend met behulp van thermodynamische gegevens ($\Delta V_\mathrm{theoretisch}$).

12 Bereken $\Delta_\mathrm{r}G^0$ (in J per mol waterstof) voor de vorming van waterstof uit de elektrolyse van water bij $298\,\mathrm{K}$. Gebruik hierbij de gegevens uit bovenstaande tabel 1.

Als je dit niet kunt berekenen, gebruik dan als gegeven in het vervolg van deze opgave de waarde $1{,}987\cdot10^{5}\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$.

13 Bereken $\Delta V_\mathrm{theoretisch}$ (in V, in drie decimalen) uit het antwoord op vraag 12.

Als je dit niet kunt berekenen, gebruik dan als gegeven in het vervolg van deze opgave de waarde $1{,}234\,\mathrm{V}$.

Wanneer bij de elektrolyse van water gebruikgemaakt wordt van een kathode van Pt en een anode van geoxideerd nikkel, $\mathrm{NiO}_x$, is de minimale spanning die moet worden toegepast ($\Delta V_\mathrm{min}$) gelijk aan $1{,}6\,\mathrm{V}$.

Het verschil tussen $\Delta V_\mathrm{min}$ en $\Delta V_\mathrm{theoretisch}$ wordt veroorzaakt door energieverliezen bij de elektrolyse.

Het thermodynamische rendement ($\eta$) bij de elektrolyse van water is het gedeelte van het vermogen dat wordt gebruikt voor de ontleding van water.

$\eta$ kan worden berekend uit $\Delta V_\mathrm{min}$ en $\Delta V_\mathrm{theoretisch}$ en wordt weergegeven als een percentage.

14 Bereken het thermodynamische rendement $\eta$ voor de elektrolyse van water waarbij gebruikgemaakt wordt van een kathode van Pt en een anode van $\mathrm{NiO}_x$.

Een alternatief voor de elektrolyse van water is de zogenoemde fotokatalytische ontleding van water. Hierbij wordt gebruikgemaakt van een foto-elektrode. Dit is vaak een halfgeleider, bijvoorbeeld $\ce{TiO2}$, die kan worden geactiveerd door de absorptie van (zon)licht.

figuur 2 schematische weergave van de fotokatalytische ontleding van water

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2022-3-3-fig2.png

In een proefopstelling werd de productie van $\ce{H2}$ onderzocht:

De foto-elektrode, met een oppervlakte van $16\,\mathrm{mm^2}$, werd belicht met gesimuleerd zonlicht bij $T = 25\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ en $p = p_0$.

Het vermogen van het invallende licht bedroeg $1{,}0\,\mathrm{kW\,m^{-2}}$.

In $1{,}0$ uur werd $0{,}37\,\mathrm{cm^3}$ waterstof geproduceerd.

15 Bereken het thermodynamische rendement ($\eta$) van deze waterstofproductie.

$20\%$ of the original amount of $\ce{N2O4}$ has dissociated and the total pressure of the equilibrium mixture is $1.01\cdot10^{5}\,\mathrm{Pa}$.

What is the equilibrium constant $K_\mathrm{p}$ of this equilibrium?

A $5.0\cdot10^{3}\,\mathrm{Pa}$
B $1.7\cdot10^{4}\,\mathrm{Pa}$
C $2.0\cdot10^{4}\,\mathrm{Pa}$
D $2.5\cdot10^{4}\,\mathrm{Pa}$
E $3.4\cdot10^{4}\,\mathrm{Pa}$
F $5.0\cdot10^{4}\,\mathrm{Pa}$

13 For a certain zeroth-order reaction, a conversion of $20$ percent is reached in $15$ minutes at $40\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

For the same reaction, a conversion of $10$ percent is reached in $1.5$ minutes at $60\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

What is the activation energy of this reaction?

A $1.0\cdot10^{3}\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$
B $1.6\cdot10^{3}\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$
C $7.0\cdot10^{4}\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$
D $1.0\cdot10^{5}\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$

14 In the upper layers of the atmosphere, ozone is converted into oxygen:

$$\ce{2 O3(g) -> 3 O2(g)}$$

A possible mechanism for this conversion is:

$$\ce{O3(g) <=> O(g) + O2(g)} \quad \text{(fast)}$$

$$\ce{O(g) + O3(g) -> 2 O2(g)} \quad \text{(slow)}$$

Which rate equation is consistent with this mechanism?

A $s=k[\ce{O3}]$
B $s=k\dfrac{[\ce{O3}]}{[\ce{O2}]}$
C $s=k[\ce{O3}]^2$
D $s=k\dfrac{[\ce{O3}]^2}{[\ce{O2}]}$

17 Potassium permanganate ($\ce{KMnO4}$) is a purple substance. A solution of potassium permanganate absorbs light with a wavelength of $525\,\mathrm{nm}$.

When an acidified solution of potassium permanganate reacts with an oxalic acid solution, $\ce{MnO4^-}$ is converted into $\ce{Mn^{2+}}$ and $\ce{H2C2O4}$ is converted into $\ce{CO2}$.

To $1.00\,\mathrm{mL}$ of an acidified $x\,\mathrm{M}$ potassium permanganate solution, $1.00\,\mathrm{mL}$ of a $y\,\mathrm{M}$ oxalic acid solution is added.

After the reaction, the absorbance of the solution is measured: $0.600$.

Then, to $1.00\,\mathrm{mL}$ of the acidified $x\,\mathrm{M}$ potassium permanganate solution, $1.50\,\mathrm{mL}$ of the $y\,\mathrm{M}$ oxalic acid solution is added.

After the reaction, the absorbance is $0.320$.

In both absorbance measurements a cuvette with a path length of $1.00\,\mathrm{cm}$ is used.

With which system of two equations in two unknowns can $x$ and $y$ be calculated? Assume that only $\ce{MnO4^-}$ absorbs light at $525\,\mathrm{nm}$.

$$\begin{array}{ll} \textbf{A} & 1.00x-0.400y=3.00\cdot10^{-4} \\ & 1.00x-0.600y=1.60\cdot10^{-4} \\ \textbf{B} & 1.00x-0.400y=6.00\cdot10^{-4} \\ & 1.00x-0.600y=4.00\cdot10^{-4} \\ \textbf{C} & 1.00x-1.00y=3.00\cdot10^{-4} \\ & 1.00x-1.50y=1.60\cdot10^{-4} \\ \textbf{D} & 1.00x-1.00y=6.00\cdot10^{-4} \\ & 1.00x-1.50y=4.00\cdot10^{-4} \\ \textbf{E} & 1.00x-2.50y=3.00\cdot10^{-4} \\ & 1.00x-3.75y=1.60\cdot10^{-4} \\ \textbf{F} & 1.00x-2.50y=6.00\cdot10^{-4} \\ & 1.00x-3.75y=4.00\cdot10^{-4} \end{array}$$

problems.title: Gold in solution
problems.problem:
Problem 2 (19 points). Gold in solution

[Open questions, total 37 points.]

Gold is a noble metal; there are almost no acids that will react with it. One of the few liquids that gold will react with is aqua regia. Aqua regia is a mixture of concentrated hydrochloric acid and concentrated nitric acid in a volume ratio of 3.0 : 1.0. The molarity of concentrated hydrochloric acid is $12\,\mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}}$ and the molarity of concentrated nitric acid is $15\,\mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}}$.

Aqua regia has a very low pH.

1 (3 points) Calculate the pH of aqua regia. Provide your answer in the correct number of significant figures. Assume that both acids are fully ionised.

When gold reacts with aqua regia, the gold is mainly converted into $\ce{AuCl4-}$ ions. Nitrogen dioxide is also produced. This is a redox reaction.

2 (3 points) Provide the equations of both half-reactions for this redox reaction and the complete reaction equation.

When you only account for the $V^0$ values of these half-reactions, which are listed in Binas or ScienceData, you could conclude that this redox reaction cannot take place.

3 (1 point) Provide a possible explanation for why this redox reaction takes place anyway.

Besides $\ce{AuCl4-}$ ions, there are also $\ce{AuCl2-}$ ions. However, $\ce{AuCl2-}$ ions are instable; at room temperature they are converted into solid gold and $\ce{AuCl4-}$. This is an equilibrium reaction. The incomplete reaction equation for this conversion is:

$$\ce{AuCl2^-(aq) <=> Au(s) + AuCl4^-(aq) + Cl^-(aq)} \qquad \text{equilibrium I}$$

The only thing missing from this equation are the coefficients.

4 (3 points) Copy the equation above to your answer sheet and complete it.

In order to determine the equilibrium constant for equilibrium I, a mixture is investigated in which equilibrium I has been established. In this equilibrium mixture, the only negative ions present are $\ce{AuCl4-}$, $\ce{AuCl2-}$ and $\ce{Cl-}$. The only positive ions present in the mixture are $\ce{H3O+}$.

First, the equilibrium mixture is filtered. Afterwards, the $[\ce{AuCl4-}]$ in the filtrate is determined. For this, an excess of potassium iodide solution is added to a 10.00 mL sample of the filtrate, which causes the following reactions:

$$\ce{AuCl4^-(aq) + 2 I^-(aq) -> AuCl2^-(aq) + I2(aq) + 2 Cl^-(aq)}$$

and

$$\ce{AuCl2^-(aq) + I^-(aq) -> AuI(s) + 2 Cl^-(aq)}$$

The iodine which is produced, is then titrated with a solution of sodium thiosulphate, which causes the following reaction:

$$\ce{2 S2O3^{2-}(aq) + I2(aq) -> S4O6^{2-}(aq) + 2 I^-(aq)}$$

This titration required 5.34 mL of a 0.0100 M sodium thiosulphate solution.

It can be assumed that the filtration, addition of potassium iodide solution, and the titration do not cause a shift of equilibrium I.

5 (3 points) Calculate the $[\ce{AuCl4-}]$ in $\mathrm{mol\,L^{-1}}$ of the investigated equilibrium mixture.

After the $[\ce{AuCl4-}]$ is known, more has to be determined in order to be able to calculate the equilibrium constant.

The $[\ce{AuCl2-}]$ in the equilibrium mixture can be calculated by filtering the mixture that was created after the titration and determining the mass of the residue. With this, and the amount of mmol of $\ce{AuCl4-}$ in the 10.00 mL sample, you can calculate how many mmol of $\ce{AuCl2-}$ were present in the 10.00 mL sample.

6 (2 points) Explain how you can calculate the amount of mmol of $\ce{AuCl2-}$ in the 10.00 mL sample, using the amount of mmol of $\ce{AuI}$ in the residue and the amount of mmol of $\ce{AuCl4-}$ in the 10.00 mL sample.

By determining the pH of the equilibrium mixture, the $[\ce{Cl-}]$ in the equilibrium mixture can be calculated. This is because the $[\ce{H3O+}]$, the $[\ce{AuCl4-}]$, the $[\ce{AuCl2-}]$ and the $[\ce{Cl-}]$ are related.

7 (2 points) What is the relation between the $[\ce{H3O+}]$, the $[\ce{AuCl4-}]$, the $[\ce{AuCl2-}]$ and the $[\ce{Cl-}]$ in the equilibrium mixture? Explain your answer.

8 (2 points) Does the concentration of $\ce{Au}$ still need to be determined in order to calculate the equilibrium constant of equilibrium I? Explain your answer.

problems.title: Click Chemistry
problems.problem:
Problem 3 (18 points). Click Chemistry

The Nobel prize for chemistry was won by Carolyn Bertozzi, Barry Sharpless and Morten Meldal in 2022 for thinking of and developing the concept of click chemistry. During click chemistry one takes two molecules and basically “clicks” them together, like you would Lego bricks.

An example of a click reaction is the one between an alkyne ($\ce{R1-C#CH}$) and an organic azide ($\ce{R2-N3}$), for the forming of a so-called triazole. If one does not utilise a specific catalyst, a mixture of two compounds is formed: the so-called anti product and the so-called syn product.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2023-1-10-fig1.png

In many cases equal amounts of the anti and syn product are formed.

9 (2 points) Is the anti product a stereoisomer of the syn product? Please explain.

When $\ce{R1}$ and/or $\ce{R2}$ are big groups (and no catalyst is used), there appears to be a preference for the forming of the anti product. This is because the large groups are in each other's way (steric hindrance). An example of one such reaction where the anti and syn products are not formed in equal amounts, is the conversion below:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2023-1-10-fig2.png

Here the anti product ($\mathbf{I}$) and the syn product ($\mathbf{II}$) are formed in a molar ratio of 1.6 : 1.0.

In an experiment in which 10 grams of the alkyne reacted with the appropriate amount of the azide, 11 grams of the anti product ($\mathbf{I}$) had formed.

10 (5 points) Calculate the percentage of the alkyne that was in total converted to both products $\mathbf{I}$ and $\mathbf{II}$.

The work that was awarded with the Nobel Prize contained, among other things, the research into catalysts that helped form specifically the anti or syn product. They discovered that by the use of a copper(I) catalyst only the anti product was formed and by the use of a ruthenium catalyst only the syn product was formed.

The production of compound $\mathbf{I}$ with a copper(I) catalyst is shown below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2023-1-10-fig3.png

If one only wants to produce the anti product $\mathbf{I}$, the reaction with the use of the copper(I) catalyst better suits the principles of Green Chemistry than the reaction without the use of a catalyst.

11 (2 points) Explain for principles 2 and 6 why the reaction with the use of the copper(I) catalyst is ‘greener’ than the reaction without a catalyst (see BINAS-table 97F or ScienceData table 38.6 or the information on page 15 of this booklet). Use information given to you in this exercise.

[Principles 2 and 6 as printed on the "Green Chemistry" information page (page 15 of the paper):]

[2. Atom economy: Synthetic methods should try to maximize the incorporation of all materials used in the process into the final product. This means that less waste will be generated as a result.]

[6. Design for energy efficiency: Energy requirements should be minimized, and processes should be conducted at ambient temperature and pressure whenever possible.]

For the azide-group of a molecule $\ce{R2-N3}$ two mesomeric structures can be drawn that comply with the octet rule. One of those structures is shown below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2023-1-10-fig4.png

12 (2 points) Draw the other mesomeric structure. If applicable, also give the formal charges.

13 (4 points) Give a possible reaction mechanism for the forming of the anti product from $\ce{R1-C#CH}$ and $\ce{R2-N3}$.
• Use the mesomeric structure of the azide given above.
• Clarify how the electron pairs move with the forming and breaking of bonds by using curved arrows [a curved-arrow symbol is printed here].
• Show all the non-bonding electron pairs in the product.

Click reactions are used to make many different chemicals. Below is given the product of a reaction that was used as a part of a study to the medicinal properties of such chemicals. To prepare this chemical, two other chemicals were used: an alkyne and a chemical which had azide groups in its molecules. A catalyst was also used for this reaction.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2023-1-10-fig5.png

14 (3 points) Provide the structural formula of the two chemicals used to synthesise the chemical with the above structural formula. Write the azide group using $\ce{N3}$. Also mention what catalyst was used during this reaction, a copper(I) catalyst or a ruthenium catalyst.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2023-2-9-fig1.png

During this synthesis route reactions occur in which stereoisomers are formed. The mixtures of stereoisomers that are formed during this synthesis route, are not separated.

1 (2 points) In which reaction(s) does the number of stereoisomers increase?

In reaction 1, first a hydroxide ion reacts with a molecule $\mathbf{1}$ to form the negative ion below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2023-2-9-fig2.png

In this ion, the negative charge is not localized on one atom, but distributed over several atoms. This can be explained with the help of resonance (mesomerism).

2 (2 points) Copy the structural formula of the negative ion and indicate with asterisks (*) which atoms, except the C atom in the formula shown above, are negatively charged.

The resultant negative ion reacts with a molecule $\mathbf{2}$.

3 (2 points) Copy the sentence below and choose the correct option between the alternatives in cursive:
The reaction of the negative ion of $\mathbf{1}$ with a molecule $\mathbf{2}$ to form molecule $\mathbf{3}$ is an addition reaction / an elimination reaction / a substitution reaction in which the negative ion of $\mathbf{1}$ functions as electrophile / nucleophile.

In reaction 2, the formed molecule $\mathbf{3}$ reacts with water, with sulfuric acid acting as catalyst. The mechanism of the reaction is described step by step below.
Step 1: the lone pair on the N atom of the CN group of $\mathbf{3}$ bonds to the $\ce{H+}$ of a $\ce{H3O+}$ ion.
Step 2: a water molecule is bonded to the C atom of the CN group, while also a neutral NH group is formed.
Step 3: exchange of a proton takes place between the formed $\ce{OH2+}$ group and the N atom.
Step 4: transfer of a proton takes place from the OH group to a water molecule, bonds also shift so that $\mathbf{4}$ is produced.

4 (8 points) Show the steps 1 to 4 of the mechanism with structural formulas.
• Use the following notations for the side chains:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2023-2-9-fig3.png

• Draw all bonding and non-bonding electron pairs.
• Use curved arrows [a curved-arrow symbol is printed here] to indicate how the electron pairs shift during the formation and breaking of bonds.
• Place all formal charges in the right place.

In reaction 3 the pyridine ring ($\ce{R2}$ in question 4) reacts with hydrogen. In this reaction, the benzene ring ($\ce{R1}$ in question 4) does not react with hydrogen. This is due to the so-called resonance energy (mesomeric energy) of both groups.
The resonance energy of the benzene ring ($1.50\cdot10^{5}\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$) is the difference between the energy released during the complete hydrogenation of three moles of $\ce{C=C}$ bonds and the energy released during the complete hydrogenation of one mole of benzene rings.
The resonance energy of the pyridine ring ($1.07\cdot10^{5}\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$) is the difference between the energy released during the complete hydrogenation of two moles of $\ce{C=C}$ bonds together with one mole of $\ce{C=N}$ bonds and the energy released during the complete hydrogenation of one mole of pyridine rings.
As an explanation for the fact that in reaction 3 the pyridine ring is hydrogenated and the benzene ring is not, Gerrit assumes that more energy is released in the reaction of the pyridine ring with hydrogen than in the reaction of the benzene ring with hydrogen.

5 (6 points) Control by means of a calculation whether during the hydrogenation of one mole of pyridine rings more energy is released than in the hydrogenation of one mole of benzene rings.

• The resonance energy of the pyridine ring is $1.07\cdot10^{5}\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$.
• During the complete hydrogenation of one mole of benzene rings, $2.1\cdot10^{5}\,\mathrm{J}$ is produced.

6 (1 point) Give another possible explanation for the fact that the benzene ring in reaction 3 is not hydrogenated.

problems.title: The decomposition of azomethane
problems.problem:
Problem 3 (14 points). The decomposition of azomethane

Azomethane has the molecular formula $\ce{C2H6N2}$. In one molecule of azomethane, there are two nitrogen atoms bonded to each other and each nitrogen atom is bonded to a methyl group.

9 (2 points) Give the Lewis structure of a molecule of azomethane. Indicate the methyl groups as $\ce{CH3}$.

10 (3 points) Explain whether stereoisomers of azomethane are possible.

Azomethane decomposes readily to form ethane and nitrogen:

$$\ce{C2H6N2(g) -> C2H6(g) + N2(g)}$$

During an investigation into the kinetics of the reaction, a certain amount of azomethane was placed in a reaction vessel with a fixed volume and the pressure in the vessel was measured a number of times. The temperature remained constant during the experiment. The following results were obtained:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline t & 10.0\ \mathrm{min} & 21.0\ \mathrm{min} & 35.0\ \mathrm{min} & \infty \\ \hline p_\text{total} & 0.656\cdot10^{5}\ \mathrm{Pa} & 0.732\cdot10^{5}\ \mathrm{Pa} & 0.813\cdot10^{5}\ \mathrm{Pa} & 1.144\cdot10^{5}\ \mathrm{Pa} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

At $t = \infty$ all azomethane has been converted.

11 (7 points) Show that the decomposition of azomethane is a first order reaction and calculate the rate constant $k$ for the reaction at this temperature.

12 (2 points) Indicate what you need to do if you want to determine the activation energy of this reaction.

problems.title: Superphosphate
problems.problem:
Problem 4 (15 points). Superphosphate

The fertilizer superphosphate is a mixture of mostly calcium hydrogen phosphate ($\ce{Ca(H2PO4)2}$) and calcium sulphate ($\ce{CaSO4}$). Superphosphate is prepared by reacting an ore, consisting mainly of fluorapatite ($\ce{Ca5(PO4)3F}$), with pure sulfuric acid at normal temperature and pressure. This reaction produces only gaseous hydrogen fluoride ($\ce{HF}$), solid calcium dihydrogen phosphate and solid calcium sulfate.

13 (3 points) Give the equation of the reaction between fluorapatite and sulfuric acid. Also indicate the states.

14 (3 points) Calculate the mass percentage of calcium dihydrogen phosphate, rounded to a whole number, in superphosphate if it were prepared from pure fluorapatite and pure sulfuric acid.

Of the ingredients in superphosphate, only calcium dihydrogen phosphate is effective as fertilizer. Calcium dihydrogen phosphate is soluble in water at room temperature. The remaining ingredients of the superphosphate can be removed by adding water to the superphosphate and then filtering the obtained cloudy liquid at room temperature.
When water is added to superphosphate, the following occurs:

$$\ce{Ca(H2PO4)2 -> Ca^{2+} + 2 H2PO4^-}$$

and

$$\ce{CaSO4 <=> Ca^{2+} + SO4^{2-}}$$

Calcium sulfate is moderately soluble in water at room temperature. When water is added to superphosphate, less calcium sulfate dissolves per liter compared to adding water to calcium sulphate alone.

15 (2 points) Explain why, when water is added to superphosphate, less calcium sulfate dissolves per liter compared to adding water to calcium sulphate alone.

Emmy wants to determine the amount of mmoles of calcium dihydrogen phosphate present in a small sample of superphoshate. Water is added to the sample until the volume of the solution is 100.0 mL. All calcium dihydrogen phosphate dissolves. After the non-dissolved components of the superphosphate have precipitated, two solutions are added in excess to 10.00 mL of the colourless solution: one of them is a solution of ammonia and the other is a solution of a molybdenum (Mo) complex. As a result, all $\ce{H2PO4-}$ ions in solution react forming solid $\ce{(NH4)3PMo12O40}$. This solid compound is removed from the suspension by means of filtration. It is then added to a solution containing 10.0 mmol dissolved NaOH. This amount of NaOH is a small excess.
Upon adding the solid to the NaOH solution, all $\ce{(NH4)3PMo12O40}$ reacts with $\ce{OH-}$. Only $\ce{MoO4^{2-}}$, $\ce{HPO4^{2-}}$, $\ce{H2O}$ and $\ce{NH3}$ are formed. Finally, after adding a suitable indicator, the amount of unreacted $\ce{OH-}$ is determined using a titration with a solution of hydrochloric acid. It turns out that 0.380 mmol $\ce{H3O+}$ ions are needed. You can assume that $\ce{H3O+}$ only reacts with $\ce{OH-}$.

To determine the amount of mmoles of calcium hydrogen phosphate in the sample of superphosphate one needs to know the molar ratio in which $\ce{(NH4)3PMo12O40}$ and $\ce{OH-}$ react. This (rather extreme) molar ratio can be found by setting up part of the reaction equation and looking at the charges left and right of the reaction arrow.

16 (3 points) Set up part of the reaction equation and explain, based on charges left and right of the reaction arrow, how many moles of $\ce{OH-}$ react with 1 mol $\ce{(NH4)3PMo12O40}$.

17 (4 points) Calculate the amount of mmoles of calcium hydrogen phosphate in the superphosphate sample.

problems.title: Lithium-ion battery
problems.problem:
Problem 1 (13 points). Lithium-ion battery

In 2019, John B. Goodenough, M. Stanley Whittingham and A. Yoshino were awarded the Nobel Prize in chemistry for the development of the lithium-ion battery. A lithium-ion battery consists of a copper electrode covered with a layer of graphite containing lithium, represented by $\ce{LiC6}$, and an aluminum electrode covered with a layer of $\ce{LiCoO2}$. The equations for the half-reactions on which the operation of the cell relies, can be shown as follows, including the corresponding standard electrode potentials under standard conditions:

$$\ce{Li+ + C6 + e- <=> LiC6}, \text{ with } V^0 = -3.05\ \mathrm{V}$$

and

$$\ce{CoO2 + Li+ + e- <=> LiCoO2}, \text{ with } V^0 = +1.00\ \mathrm{V}$$

1 (2 points) Write down the equation of the complete reaction when a lithium-ion battery provides a current.

2 (1 point) Calculate the cell potential of a fully charged battery under standard conditions.

3 (3 points) Give the charges of the particles in the $\ce{CoO2}$ and the $\ce{LiCoO2}$. Indicate these charges in the sentences on the answer sheet.

[Sentences printed on the answer sheet:]
In $\ce{CoO2}$: the charge of Co is ….. and the charge of O is …..
In $\ce{LiCoO2}$: the charge of Li is ….., the charge of Co is ….. and the charge of O is ……

An important characteristic of a battery is its capacity. This is measured in mAh.

4 (3 points) Calculate the minimum amount of lithium in g that is required to be present in a lithium-ion battery to deliver a current of 200 mA over 2 days.

Based on the same principle of the lithium-ion battery, it should be possible to make a battery using magnesium instead.

We compare such a magnesium-ion battery with a lithium-ion battery. When fully charged, there are equal amounts in gram of the metal in both batteries. We allow both batteries to provide the same constant current until they are fully discharged.

5 (4 points) Explain which battery is able to provide power for the longest period of time and calculate the mathematical ratio between the times of the two different batteries (to full discharge).

Consider the following general chemical reaction in aqueous environment:

Problem 6 (14 points). Synthesis of Oseltamivir

Oseltamivir is a registered medicine (Tamiflu®) that is used to treat the influenza virus. Due to the importance of this medicine, multiple pathways for the synthesis of Oseltamivir have been developed. The first part of one of these pathways is provided below and begins with shikimic acid ($\mathbf{1}$), that is isolated from star anise.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2023-3-6-fig1.png

During the conversion of shikimic acid ($\mathbf{1}$) to compound $\mathbf{A}$, ethanol is both reagent and solvent. A limited amount of thionyl chloride ($\ce{SOCl2}$) is gradually added to a mixture of ethanol and shikimic acid.
The reaction between ethanol and thionyl chloride produces hydrogen chloride, which acts as a catalyst in the formation of $\mathbf{A}$ from shikimic acid and ethanol.
Then $\mathbf{A}$ reacts with pentane-3-one under the influence of an acid catalyst to form compound $\mathbf{B}$.
Finally, $\ce{CH3SO2Cl}$ is used to prepare compound $\mathbf{2}$ in the presence of triethylamine.

The reaction of ethanol with thionyl chloride produces two other compounds other than hydrogen chloride.

28 (2 points) Give the formulas of these two compounds.

A procedure for the conversion of shikimic acid to $\mathbf{A}$ is described below:

In a 250 mL round-bottom flask, equipped with a reflux condenser and a magnetic stirrer, under an atmosphere of an inert gas, 19.90 g (= 0.114 mol) shikimic acid is suspended in 80 mL (= 1.4 mol) ethanol. To this mixture 4.16 mL (= 0.057 mol) thionyl chloride is added gradually over the course of 10 minutes. The mixture is refluxed for 2 hours, after which compound $\mathbf{A}$ is isolated with a 98% yield.

Due to the presence of OH groups in the shikimic acid molecule, thionyl chloride can react with ethanol as well as with shikimic acid. Whether that reaction affects the final yield of $\mathbf{A}$ depends on the type of OH groups in shikimic acid that react.

When the reaction takes place with the OH group of the COOH group, it has no influence on the yield of $\mathbf{A}$.
When the reaction takes place with the alcoholic OH groups, it does have an influence on the yield of $\mathbf{A}$.

29 (2 points) Explain why the reaction between thionyl chloride with shikimic acid, via the OH of the COOH group, has no influence on the yield of $\mathbf{A}$.

30 (3 points) Explain that, for the reaction with thionyl chloride, it can be deduced from the data in the above description that the reactivity of the OH groups of ethanol is greater than the reactivity of the alcoholic OH groups of shikimic acid.

31 (2 points) Give the formula of $\mathbf{Z}$.

32 (2 points) Explain, using the diagram, whether the reaction of $\mathbf{A}$ with pentan-3-one is regio selective.

33 (3 points) Explain whether the ‘lower’ C atom (to which the $\ce{-OSO2CH3}$ group is attached) in the six-membered ring of compound $\mathbf{2}$ has the $R$- or $S$-configuration. Use a sketch in your explanation.

Problem 7 (17 points). Oseltamivir determination

Oseltamivir is sold as the water-soluble salt of phosphoric acid, oseltamivir phosphate:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2023-3-7-fig1.png

From here on, oseltimivir phosphate will be represented as $\ce{OsH^+H2PO4^-}$.

In order to guarantee the quality of oseltamivir phosphate, the purity of the product must be checked regularly. This can be done, for example, by first converting the oseltamivir phosphate to oseltamivir chloride, $\ce{OsH^+Cl^-}$. Excess caustic soda (a solution of NaOH) is added to a solution of this compound and finally a titration with hydrochloric acid is performed.

$\ce{OsH^+Cl^-}$ dissolves as follows:

$$\ce{OsH^+Cl^- -> OsH+ + Cl-}$$

$\ce{OsH+}$ is a weak acid, with $\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a} = 7.90$. When caustic soda is added, the following reaction occurs:

$$\ce{OsH+ + OH- -> Os + H2O}$$

In such a determination, the oseltamivir phosphate from one 75.0 mg capsule is completely converted to oseltamivir chloride. This is dissolved in demineralized water and then the solution is filled to a final volume of 50.0 mL. Then 1,00 mL $5.00\cdot10^{-2}$ M caustic soda is added to 10.0 mL of this solution. The excess caustic soda is then back-titrated with $1.00\cdot10^{-3}$ M hydrochloric acid, of which 13.6 mL was required.

34 (6 points) Calculate the mass percentage of the oseltamivir phosphate in the capsule. Assume that the ester bond does not react during the addition of the caustic soda and the titration process.

Phenolphthalein is used as indicator during the back-titration.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2023-3-7-fig2.png

A titration curve for a solution of oseltamivir phosphate with caustic soda was established based on a $\mathrm{p}K\mathrm{a}$ of 7.90 for the $\ce{OsH+}$ to investigate if the determination could also be carried out by dissolving the capsule containing the oseltamivir phosphate in water and titrating the solution directly.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2023-3-7-fig3.png

A peculiar aspect of this titration curve is that there is only one steep area, despite $\ce{OsH^+H2PO4^-}$ being a triprotic acid.

37 (2 points) Explain why there is only one steep area in the titration curve when oseltamivir phosphate is titrated with caustic soda, despite oseltamivir phosphate being a triprotic acid

The titration curve above shows that it is possible to titrate a solution of oseltamivir phosphate directly with caustic soda.

38 (3 points) Using the titration curve above, explain that it is possible to titrate a solution of oseltamivir phosphate directly with caustic soda; also indicate which indicator you might use and give the color change of that indicator at the equivalence point.

39 (1 point) Indicate the molar ratio for $\ce{OsH^+H2PO4^-}:\ce{OH-}$ during the direct titration of a solution of oseltamivir phosphate with caustic soda.

Problem 2 (11 points). Determining manganese levels in tea leaves

[Open questions, total 27 points.]

Tea leaves contain small amounts of manganese; less than 0.1 percent by mass. The manganese exclusively occurs in the form of $\ce{Mn^{2+}}$ ions. The content of manganese in tea leaves can be determined using colorimetry. Because $\ce{Mn^{2+}}$ does not produce any colour in aqueous solutions, it should first be converted into permanganate ($\ce{MnO4-}$).
Permanganate ions cause a purple coloration in water. For this conversion, periodate ($\ce{IO4-}$) is used, which is converted to iodate ($\ce{IO3-}$):

$$\ce{2 Mn^{2+} + 5 IO4- + 3 H2O -> 2 MnO4- + 5 IO3- + 6 H+}$$

1 (3 points) Give the equation of the half-reaction for the conversion of periodate to iodate.

For the determination of the $\ce{Mn^{2+}}$ content of tea leaves, the periodate must be added in excess. In such a determination, 2 to 3 grams of tea leaves and roughly 0.5 g of potassium periodate are used.

2 (4 points) Show by calculation that adding 0.5 g of potassium periodate is more than enough to get all the $\ce{Mn^{2+}}$ in tea leaves to react. Assume that the tea leaves contain 0.1 percent $\ce{Mn^{2+}}$ by mass.

For a colorimetric determination of the manganese content of tea leaves, a series of solutions is first made with $\ce{MnO4-}$ contents of 0.800, 0.600, 0.400, 0.200 and $0.100\,\mathrm{mmol\,L^{-1}}$.
For each of these solutions, the color intensity is measured using a colorimeter. These color intensities are then graphed against the $\ce{MnO4-}$ content in $\mathrm{mmol\,L^{-1}}$. This graph is shown below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2024-1-10-fig1.png

For the determination of the mass percentage of $\ce{Mn^{2+}}$ in Earl Grey tea leaves the following steps were taken:
1. 2.580 g of tea leaves were heated in a porcelain crucible.
2. The resulting ashes were heated with an amount of 4 M sulfuric acid solution.
3. Afterwards, the mixture was filtered.
4. 0.50 g potassium periodate was added to the filtrate.
5. When the reaction was complete, the entire mixture was transferred into a 50 mL volumetric flask. In the flask, demineralized water was added up to the mark.
6. Finally, the intensity of the purple colour of this solution was measured: 0.140.

3 (4 points) Calculate the mass percentage of $\ce{Mn^{2+}}$ in the examined tea leaves.

problems.title: Vasa
problems.problem:
Problem 3 (16 points). Vasa

Epoxyalkanes are compounds that can be thought of as being derived from alkanes by replacing per molecule two H atoms on two different C atoms with one O atom. Examples of epoxyalkanes are:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2024-1-11-fig1.png

Epoxyalkanes in which the oxygen atom in the molecules is bonded to two adjacent carbon atoms can easily polymerize under the influence of sodium hydroxide. This produces polyepoxyethane from epoxyethane. This polymer is often used to preserve wooden ships that have been under water for a very long time. This happened, among other things, with the Swedish warship Vasa, which capsized in the Stockholm harbor on its maiden voyage in 1628. From April 1961, when the ship resurfaced, it was treated with polyepoxyethane for 17 years.

A molecule of polyepoxyethane can be represented as follows:

$$\mathrm{H{-}(O{-}CH_2{-}CH_2)}_{n}\mathrm{{-}OH}$$

The value of $n$ in this formula can vary from less than 10 to more than 100. The formation of such a polymer molecule follows a mechanism with a number of successive steps.

The first step (initiation) is the attachment of a hydroxide ion to an epoxyethane molecule:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/chemistry-olympiads-bank/main/images/nl-2024-1-11-fig2.png

Then, starting from ion A, a number of successive propagation steps take place. A negative ion is formed again and again.

4 (3 points) Starting from ion A, show the first two successive propagation steps in structural formulas.

1,2-epoxypropane can also polymerize under the influence of sodium hydroxide. This polymerization proceeds by the same mechanism as the polymerization of epoxyethane.

5 (3 points) Show a part of the middle of a polymer molecule of poly-1,2-epoxypropane in structural formula. This part must be composed of three monomer units.

In polymerizations of epoxyalkanes, a series of successive propagation steps is terminated by a reaction with a water molecule (termination reaction). Research into the polymerization of epoxyethane under the influence of sodium hydroxide showed that, depending on the conditions under which the polymerization is carried out, different types of polyepoxyethane with different melting ranges can be obtained.

In one of the experiments in this study, an amount of polyepoxyethane with a mass of 92 grams was formed from 88 grams of epoxyethane. In this experiment there was no epoxyethane left at the end.

6 (3 points) Give the reaction equation for the mentioned termination reaction. Use the formula $\mathrm{H{-}(O{-}CH_2{-}CH_2)}_{n}\mathrm{{-}OH}$ for the end product.

7 (4 points) Calculate the average value of $n$ in the polyepoxyethane molecules $\mathrm{H{-}(O{-}CH_2{-}CH_2)}_{n}\mathrm{{-}OH}$ that are formed during the experiments described above.

Two other experiments from this study are described below.

$$\begin{array}{l|c|c|c} & & \text{fabric used} & \\ \hline & \text{epoxyethane (mol)} & \ce{NaOH}\ \text{(mol)} & \ce{H2O}\ \text{(mol)} \\ \hline \text{experiment 1} & 1.0 & 0.036 & 0.33 \\ \hline \text{experiment 2} & 1.0 & 0.036 & 0.10 \end{array}$$

Both experiments took place at the same temperature and pressure.
After polymerization of all epoxyethane, the polyepoxyethane was separated from the resulting reaction mixture. One of the experiments showed that polyepoxyethane was formed with a melting range of $+2\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $+4\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$, while in the other experiment the melting range of the resulting polyepoxyethane was $+31\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $+33\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$.

8 (3 points) Explain which of the two experiments produced polyepoxyethane with the highest melting range.
